text.tspan: Public opinion on common farming practices in the UK
Survey responses from about 1,000 UK adults in 2022 on their views of common farming practices.
Acceptable
Killing newborn chicks using CO₂ gassing or
meat-grinders
Keeping chickens in cages with about the space of
an A4 sheet of printer paper per bird
Cutting the beaks of newborn chicks
Castrating newborn calves by cutting or crushing the
testicles
Removing calves' horn buds using hot iron
Killing newborn male calves as they cannot produce
milk
Cutting or grinding the teeth of newborn piglets
Cutting the tails off newborn piglets
Keeping pigs in cages in which they cannot turn
around for several weeks
Not acceptable
Killing newborn chicks using CO₂ gassing or
meat-grinders
Keeping chickens in cages with about the space of
an A4 sheet of printer paper per bird
Cutting the beaks of newborn chicks
Castrating newborn calves by cutting or crushing the
testicles
Removing calves' horn buds using hot iron
Killing newborn male calves as they cannot produce
milk
Cutting or grinding the teeth of newborn piglets
Cutting the tails off newborn piglets
Keeping pigs in cages in which they cannot turn
around for several weeks
Don't know / no opinion
Killing newborn chicks using CO₂ gassing or
meat-grinders
Keeping chickens in cages with about the space of
an A4 sheet of printer paper per bird
Cutting the beaks of newborn chicks
Castrating newborn calves by cutting or crushing the
testicles
Removing calves' horn buds using hot iron
Killing newborn male calves as they cannot produce
milk
Cutting or grinding the teeth of newborn piglets
Cutting the tails off newborn piglets
Keeping pigs in cages in which they cannot turn
around for several weeks
